campaign_name: Initiative Petition 26-02: income tax rate 5% to 4% by tax year 2031 (2028 ballot)
purpose: Phase the state personal income tax rate down from 5% to 4% by tax year 2031
sponsor: Brian Shortsleeve (former gubernatorial candidate), per Foley Hoag
signatures_required: 74,574 (no more than 25% from one county under MA rules); second round of 12,429 later if Legislature does not act (2026-cycle figure)
deadline: Nov 18, 2026 to local clerks; Dec 2, 2026 to Secretary of State
evidence_note: Certified by AG Sept 2026 as one of 14 petitions for 2028. Only petition where Foley Hoag names a proponent. No source found on a committee, funding, signature firm or signature progress. Pending MA legislation (Senate passed; House planned vote June 2026) would ban per-signature pay and require 'paid individual' disclosure on petitions — enactment status unverified.

campaign_name: Initiative Petition 26-08: data center regulation (2028 ballot)
purpose: Regulate data center construction, expansion and operation; Ballotpedia says it would require local voter approval and other conditions for data center permits
sponsor: Jim Fleming of West Springfield (filed personally), per Boston.com
circulation_firm: Possibly JEF Associates (Fleming's own company, which sells certified-signature/ballot-initiative services) — not confirmed as hired for this petition
deadline: Nov 18, 2026 to local clerks; Dec 2, 2026 to Secretary of State
evidence_note: Certified by AG. Boston.com says funding was not disclosed and gives no paid/volunteer plan. The proponent runs a signature-services business, so this is worth a direct outreach, but there is no evidence of a paying client.

campaign_name: SignatureDrive.com 'speculative' 2028 petitions (incl. 26-06 legislative employee bargaining and 26-12 end gas tax)
purpose: Harold Hubschman filed about 10 questions for 2028 (examples: let legislative staffers unionize; eliminate the gas tax) to pitch to potential backers
sponsor: No backer identified. Boston Globe (Sept 22, 2026): Hubschman 'hasn't actually gotten anyone to pick up the proposals'
circulation_firm: SignatureDrive.com (Harold Hubschman) is the filer and would be the firm
deadline: Nov 18, 2026 to local clerks; Dec 2, 2026 to Secretary of State
budget_or_spend: No 2028 spend reported. For 2026-cycle context, SignatureDrive.com took in at least $4.6M since the start of 2025 (incl. >$1M from CPCS union committee; >$1.4M from Legalize Starter Homes, paid to the firm or others)
website: https://signaturedrive.com (named in Boston Globe; site not checked)
evidence_note: The Globe names only 2 of the 10 topics; which certified numbers are Hubschman's beyond 26-06 and 26-12 is unverified. With no paying client as of Sept 22, 2026, these may not circulate at scale.

purpose: 26-01 non-ionizing radiation research office; 26-05 state employee collective bargaining; 26-09 1% internet ad tax; 26-10 clean-energy income tax credit; 26-11 eliminate legislative stipends; 26-14 and 26-15 property tax cap at 102.5% (versions A and B); 26-16 larceny felony at $250; 26-17 sales tax 6.25% to 5%; 26-18 hardship license pathway
sponsor: unknown (not named in Foley Hoag summary; some may be among Hubschman's 10)
deadline: Nov 18, 2026 to local clerks; Dec 2, 2026 to Secretary of State
contact: MA AG Government Bureau / Secretary of State Elections Division (public offices) for proponent filings
evidence_note: Out of 14 certified petitions, no source found reports a paying sponsor or paid firm for any of them. The proponents' names are in the AG's petition filings on mass.gov, which were not fetched here. Another round of petitions can be filed with the AG until Aug 4, 2027.

campaign_name: Referendum to repeal/suspend 2026 abortion law (Compassionate Care Coalition)
purpose: Repeal the abortion law Gov. Healey signed Aug 10, 2026 (removes post-24-week restrictions) via a 2028 ballot question; suspend it if enough signatures
sponsor: Compassionate Care Coalition, formed by Massachusetts Citizens for Life and Massachusetts Family Action; committee chair Sam Miele
signatures_required: 37,289 for ballot; 49,719 to suspend the law
deadline: Oct 23, 2026 to local clerks (passed); Nov 6, 2026 to Secretary of State
evidence_note: This is not one of the 14 initiatives; it is a separate referendum. Collection in the field has ended (local deadline was Oct 23); only filing with the Secretary of State remains. No source says whether gatherers were paid or volunteer.

campaign_name: MA circulator job ads (The Outreach Team for Coalition for Healthy Democracy / Protect Democracy)
purpose: Paid signature gathering for 2026-cycle MA initiatives (all-party primaries, public records)
deadline: n/a
pay_rate: $20-$23/hr circulator; $22-$23/hr team lead; daily bonuses up to $170 (Boston and Amherst listings); $18/hr support staff
evidence_note: No current (Oct 2026) MA circulator ad with pay was found on ZipRecruiter or in job-board searches. Indeed, Craigslist and Facebook could not be searched directly. The listings found are from the 2025 cycle and are closed or old (two board listings carry a 2022 posting date). They are useful only as pay benchmarks.

campaign_name: Initiative 87: DC Living Wage for All ($25 minimum wage)
purpose: Raise DC minimum wage to $25 by July 1, 2029 and phase out tipped subminimum by 2031
sponsor: One Fair Wage (president Saru Jayaraman); proposer Trupti Patel per 51st
signatures_required: About 26,000 per Hoodline (5% of registered voters citywide and in 5 of 8 wards)
deadline: 180 days from petition adoption (exact date unknown); target is a 2027 DC special election
signatures_collected: unknown (organizers declined to say for the first attempt)
hiring_link: Volunteer shift signup via Mobilize on https://onefairwage.org/dc (no paid positions listed)
decision_maker: Saru Jayaraman, President, One Fair Wage
contact: One Fair Wage, 275 7th Ave, 15th Floor, New York, NY 10001
evidence_note: Missed the Nov 2026 ballot. The OFW site says collection is underway for a 2027 special election; Jayaraman said collection would start July 2026. No evidence of paid circulators (sign-up is volunteer shifts). DC non-resident circulators must register with BOE before circulating.

campaign_name: Initiative 88: Rent Control and Housing Eligibility Adjustment Amendment Act of 2026 (rent freeze)
purpose: Two-year rent freeze on multifamily housing, plus extra 12-month freezes when DC-area CPI exceeds 5%
signatures_required: About 24,000 valid (5% of registered voters citywide, incl. 5% in 5 of 8 wards)
deadline: 180 days from final approval once litigation clears; earliest ballot is the expected spring 2027 special election
evidence_note: Litigation blocked collection. A challenge led by the DC Building Industry Association coalition was denied as untimely on Sept 16, 2026; an appeal was filed Sept 18. Whether circulation has started is unknown. Opposition (DCBIA, NAR) is well funded, so a well-funded drive is plausible, but that is not confirmed.

campaign_name: Other proposed DC initiatives at BOE hearing stage (DC Equal Homeownership Act; Vermelle Paid Maternity Leave Act; DC Cash Payment Reparations Act; Human Environment 'Block Up Plan')
purpose: Various; only hearing notices and advisory opinions are posted
signatures_required: 5% of registered voters citywide and in 5 of 8 wards (about 24,000)
deadline: 180 days after petition adoption (not yet adopted / unknown)
evidence_note: These are listed on the BOE Current Measures page with no proposer or circulation dates shown. Approval for circulation is not confirmed. DC Referendum 009 (tipped wage timeline, Oct 2025) and Initiative 84 (Time Stability) also appear there; their current status was not verified.

campaign_name: Initiative 86: Prohibiting the Force-Feeding of Birds (foie gras ban)
purpose: Ban sale of foie gras produced by force-feeding
deadline: Qualified Aug 5, 2026; on Nov 3, 2026 ballot
evidence_note: Collection is complete. Included as a reference point for what a DC drive takes (198 circulators, 14 weeks, record-setting signature count).

campaign_name: Salisbury collective bargaining ordinance repeal referendum (AFSCME)
purpose: Put the City Council's May 2026 repeal of the union/collective-bargaining ordinance to voters
sponsor: AFSCME Maryland (AFSCME Maryland Petitioning Project); Shore Progress also involved
circulation_firm: The Outreach Team (job ad for the AFSCME Maryland Petitioning Project, Salisbury)
signatures_required: About 4,036 (5,818 valid was 1,782 over the requirement)
deadline: Petition drive done (37 days); Council placed it on the ballot Aug 10, 2026; vote Nov 2, 2027
hiring_link: https://www.theoutreachteam.net/interest-form-tot (June 2026 posting, positions ran through June 19, possible extension)
evidence_note: Confirmed paid (job ad posted June 4, 2026), but collection is finished. The job-ad text also mentions 'campaign finance reform', which looks inconsistent. Election campaign work possible ahead of Nov 2, 2027.

campaign_name: County spending cap charter amendment (Committee to Control MoCo Spending) — 2028 retry
purpose: Charter amendment requiring unanimous Council vote for budget increases above inflation
sponsor: Committee to Control MoCo Spending (Montgomery County GOP committee)
deadline: unknown (2028 election target)
signatures_collected: 2026 attempt: >14,000 submitted, 302 short of valid; failed Aug 17, 2026
evidence_note: The committee said: 'We are planning on a new ballot petition in support of the same charter amendment for the 2028 election.' It also filed for judicial review of the 2026 count. It fell short by only 302 signatures, which makes it a strong prospect for a professional validation/QC pitch.

campaign_name: Frederick County data center zoning referendum
purpose: Referendum on county data center overlay zoning
sponsor: Frederick County Data Center Referendum Committee (DCRC); circulators paid through Envision Frederick County using a $10,000 Chesapeake Climate Action Network grant
circulation_firm: None named (paid via Envision Frederick County)
deadline: Struck by Maryland Supreme Court June 30, 2026
evidence_note: Petition ruled ineligible because the color maps were printed in black and white. WYPR says other counties have asked the DCRC for advice on their own data-center referendums, which signals possible future MD county demand for professional petition compliance.

campaign_name: 2027 candidate designating and independent nominating petitions (NYC Council, local offices)
purpose: Ballot access for 2027 primary/general candidates
signatures_required: Per NY Election Law 6-136 by office (not verified for 2027)
deadline: unknown — the 2027 NYS political calendar was not found; the brief's estimate is that petitioning starts around late Feb 2027
pay_rate: unknown for 2027. Benchmark: Green Party of NY paid $25/hr in 2024 (5 weeks)
contact: NYS Board of Elections / NYC Board of Elections (vote.nyc)
evidence_note: No 2027 calendar or 2027 job ads verified. NY has no statewide citizen initiative. The paid-petitioning market is candidate ballot access, concentrated Feb-Apr. Bills S6996/A1223 (2025) affecting petitioning exist, but their content was not verified.

campaign_name: Anti-insider-trading home rule charter amendments

deadline: Filed by Aug 4, 2026; on Nov 3, 2026 ballot
evidence_note: Collection is complete. Paid or volunteer gatherers not reported. A repeat sponsor of county charter petitions in PA, so a prospect for future work. No active or upcoming PA paid project was verified.
